regime: Risk-Off Trend Day (Nasdaq and S&P Lose Stops, Gold Falls Too)
summary: Risk came off hard. The Nasdaq followed through on Wednesday's stop loss and dropped 1.81 percent to 29,217.75, closing near the session low after a late flush to 29,111. The S&P lost its own trend stop too, down 0.65 percent to 7,710.25, so both indexes now sit below their ATR stops together. December gold did not hedge the drop, falling 1.18 percent to 4,033.3 and losing its stop. Only crude held a bid, up 0.91 percent to 102.87. VIX rose 1.71 percent to 17.21. The day after the Fed turned into broad de-risking, not a relief bounce.

event.name: No scheduled release (post-FOMC digestion; mega-cap earnings backdrop)
event.consensus: No confirmed tier-one US release. GDP and PCE remain delayed under the federal shutdown, so the tape traded on positioning and earnings rather than data.
event.actual: A broad risk-off follow-through the day after the Fed. The Nasdaq fell 1.81 percent to 29,217.75 and lost its stop; the S&P fell 0.65 percent to 7,710.25 and lost its stop; December gold fell 1.18 percent to 4,033.3 and lost its stop; crude rose 0.91 percent to 102.87.
event.surprise: No data surprise. The move was trend and positioning. Wednesday's spike-and-reverse rolled into a clean de-risk, which is why the broken stops matter more than any headline.
event.nqReaction: NQ held a wide opening range into midday, failed an up-break at 15:30 UTC (29,676.75 high), then broke down late and closed 29,217.75, below the range and below NYVWAP 29,529.80, near the 29,111 low.
event.crossAsset: MES minus 0.65 percent at 7,710.25. December gold minus 1.18 percent at 4,033.3. Crude plus 0.91 percent at 102.87. VIX 17.21, up 1.71 percent.

risk.sizing: Measured: 1 micro per strategy, with the trend. Short the names below their stops (MNQ, MES, December gold); crude is the lone long above its stop. Do not fade the fresh downtrend without a reclaim. Lines: MNQ back above 29,615; MES above 7,765; gold above 4,061; crude holds above 100.95.
risk.openRisk: Measured and trend-aligned short across equities and gold. Volatility expanded, so keep size down.
risk.note: Throttle holds at REDUCED. The systematic read is clean and short, which is tradeable, but VIX rose and realized range expanded, so this stays REDUCED rather than NORMAL. A further VIX spike moves it to DEFENSIVE. Week ahead: Friday is month-end with possible rebalancing flows; PCE and other federal data remain delayed under the shutdown; mega-cap earnings reactions stay the main Nasdaq catalyst.

psychology: Yesterday the lesson was do not chase the first spike. Today the lesson is respect a broken stop. The Nasdaq lost its trend line into Wednesday's close, and anyone who wanted to buy the dip got run over as the stop flip kept working. When the lead index flips short, the easy trade is with the new direction, not against it. Fading a fresh downtrend because it feels oversold is how a small loss becomes a big one. Let the stop do its job; the trend is down until price reclaims the line.
